gates.row_count: Counted ink against the ruled grid on the 200 dpi renders: p2 has ink on the first 2 writing lines only (row 2's address wraps to a third line carrying ONLY a ZIP, which is a wrapped address continuation and not a row - it was discarded at read time, not emitted); 2 rows emitted. p3 has ink on the first 4 writing lines only; 4 rows emitted. The single-cell geometry proof (first row, last row, one pitch past) independently confirms no dropped or duplicated line on either page.
gates.geometry_proof: p2: row1 box (x80%,y14.09%,w18%,h1.60%) renders '$268.22'; row2 box (y15.70%) renders '$1,802.45'; control one pitch below (y17.42%) renders EMPTY. p3: row1 box (y13.24%) renders '1,451 -'; row4 box (y19.79%) renders '350 -'; control one pitch below (y21.97%) renders EMPTY. NOTE: an earlier proof pass at x=84% clipped the leading '$1,' and '1,' off the wider figures - the band was widened to x=80%,w=18% and re-proved, which is exactly the shifted/short-box failure this check exists to catch.
gates.balance_chain: Cover line 4 is a bare dash in all three columns, so it is recorded BLANK ('') per the zero-glyph ruling, NOT as 0 - a bare dash is not a numeral. The chain nonetheless closes on the filer's own figures and explains the dash: cumulative contributions 16,439.41 + 60.00 = 16,499.41, cumulative expenses 16,499.41, difference exactly 0.00. Nothing was written into the blank cell. This chunk holds no earlier Swink filing, so the cross-filing chain test could not be run; the cover's LAST-REPORT column (14,368.74 / 25 / 14,368.74) is the hook for it.
